task: Add a new "unhealthy" delivery-health reason that distinguishes genuinely backend-unreachable classification holds from by-design/backend-configured holds in the OTLP spool, surfaced in `codemie proxy status` / `codemie proxy analytics status`, without false-positiving on legitimate holds.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches 4 components across 3 layers: local evidence/session hold decision (session-project.ts + tick-processor.ts), backend-capability exposure (policy-cache.ts, which no health/status consumer reads today), delivery/forwarder false-positive fix (delivery-summary.ts / delivery-state.ts), and the CLI presentation layer's new reason (delivery-health.ts). All four flow through exhaustive, compile-time-enforced reason-keyed maps (HOLD_REASONS/LOSS_REASONS in session-project.ts, DELIVERY_REASONS in delivery-health.ts) shared across many consumers, which is a core shared utility touch.

Core intent is clear (add an 'unhealthy' reason without false-positiving), but the technical analysis surfaces open design decisions: `publication_stopped` is not purely by-design (it also absorbs an expired, genuinely-stalled `publication_contract_unavailable` hold after 24h), `publication_contract_unavailable`/`organization_encoding_unsupported` each have two indistinguishable causes from `status.holds.session` alone, and the prior round-3 revert of a closely related `not_delivered` design carries no preserved rationale — the analysis explicitly recommends asking the user rather than re-deriving it.

No exact precedent for reading the per-namespace policy-cache capability file from a health collector that has never read it before, or for tagging `HoldReason`s as backend-confirmed vs backend-unconfirmed; this closely related area already went through 3 rounds of HITL spec revision and one revert. Existing patterns (reason-keyed exhaustive Records, pure-decision functions in tick-processor.ts) cover much of the mechanics, but the disambiguation logic itself is new.

3 layers touched: local evidence/session (Service), persisted `status.holds.session`/policy-cache state (DB-Persistence, with a shape extension to distinguish hold causes), and CLI presentation (`proxy status` / `proxy analytics status`). No new external integration or additional backend call is required.
